description: This course examines the meanings of sound in technological modernity through examples from the German-speaking world. German industry has long been at the forefront of recording devices, hearing aids, headphones, and synthesizers. Yet Germany has produced just as many works of fiction and nonfiction on urban noise, propaganda, and the intrusion of machines into human domains. Students develop their critical ear by listening to music and poetry, and learn to interpret visual and literary works with the minds ear. In addition to technology, the course explores how sound interacts with gender, cultural politics, medicine, and spirituality. Taught in English.
fullname: Topics in German Arts (Taught in English)
